title: Stump v. Sparkman (435 U.S. 349): The Supreme Court of the United States hands down a 5–3 decision, in a controversial case involving involuntary sterilization and judicial immunity.
text: Judicial immunity is a form of sovereign immunity, which protects judges and others employed by the judiciary from liability resulting from their judicial actions. It is intended to ensure that judges can make decisions free from improper influence exercised on them, contributing to the impartiality of the judiciary and the rule of law.

title: New Zealand National Airways Corporation (the domestic airline of New Zealand) is merged with New Zealand's international airline, Air New Zealand.
text: Air New Zealand is the flag carrier of New Zealand. Based in Auckland, the airline operates scheduled passenger flights to 20 domestic and 28 international destinations in 18 countries, primarily within the Pacific Rim.

title: Dick Smith of Dick Smith Foods tows a fake iceberg to Sydney Harbour.
text: Richard Harold Smith is an Australian entrepreneur and aviator. He is the founder of Dick Smith Electronics, Australian Geographic and Dick Smith Foods.

title: The Philippine College of Commerce, through a presidential decree, is converted to the Polytechnic University of the Philippines.
text: The Polytechnic University of the Philippines is a public research university in the Philippines with a main campus in Santa Mesa, Manila. It was founded on 19 October 1904, as the Manila Business School (MBS) and as part of Manila's public school system.

title: Dallas debuts on CBS, and gives birth to the modern day primetime soap opera.
text: CBS Broadcasting Inc. is an American commercial broadcast television network and the flagship property of the CBS Entertainment Group division of Skydance.
